title: attenuated-threshold-ward-and-geo-degradation-corridor: reduce oscillation during regional overloads
author: Amina Patel
release_notes: Introduce an attenuated threshold ward and geo degradation corridor to reduce rapid regional oscillations during overloads; configurable via runtime flags; safe rollback via feature flag.
description:
Context: recent incidents showed rapid cross-region thrash when regional health probes flipped aggressively — customers observed bursty latency and transient SLO violations during reclaim cycles. Motivation: instead of hard-circuiting or aggressive evictions we need a staged, telemetry-driven derating layer that smooths tenant weight and a geo-aware corridor that allows gradual performance degradation in the affected region while preserving global stability.

What this PR does: introduces two cooperating mechanisms: (1) 'attenuated threshold ward' — a per-tenant soft-derate controller that reduces admission weight progressively when latency/p95 or error-rate thresholds are crossed, with exponential cool-down/backoff to avoid flip-flop; (2) 'geo degradation corridor' — a region-scoped hysteresis window that restricts full hard-fallback (region ejection) and instead routes a configurable fraction of traffic to standby regions while preserving in-region KV cache for warm paths. Both mechanisms are feature-flagged and use existing SLO metrics from the telemetry pipeline.

Key behaviors: single-digit percent traffic re-route during early violation window; soft-derate is additive with existing tenant quotas but never fully denies traffic; corridor enforces a staggered ramp of cross-region failover over a time window (configured by corridor.window_ms) and only escalates to hard circuit open after sustained violations beyond corridor.max_streak.

Changes included (high level): added Ward controller (pkg/ward/controller.go), runtime config + feature flag (config/ward.yaml, infra/fflags.go), corridor coordinator (pkg/geo/corridor.go), new metrics and traces (telemetry/ward_metrics.go), unit and integration tests (pkg/ward/*_test.go, test/e2e/geo_corridor_test.go), and small dispatcher changes to consult the ward before admission (runtime/dispatcher/adm.go). Documentation: docs/ops/attenuated-ward.md and runbook updates for incident response.

Rollout plan: gated feature flag off by default. Canary run in staging for 48h, followed by progressive enablement: 5% of main region traffic -> 25% -> 100% with observability gates. Automated canary checks require no p95 regression >5% and no error-rate spike >1% absolute.

Rollback plan: flip feature flag off; corridor immediately reverts to previous routing behavior. Ward changes are additive and will decay, but an immediate disable is available.

Telemetry and observability: new telemetry.histogram 'ward.soft_derate' and gauge 'corridor.active_window' added; added a dedicated dashboard and alert 'Ward:SustainedDerate' that triggers when derate > 20% for > 10m.

Related: ENG-4821 (stability roadmap), SRE-1100 (regional failover hardening), SUP-3412 (customer incident inbound).
commits:
1) add ward controller and model + tests
2) add geo corridor coordinator and config hooks
3) dispatcher hooks and telemetry plumbing
4) docs and runbook updates
5) adjust unit tests and fix flake in admission path
6) bump e2e canary to include corridor scenario
review_comments:
Diego Morales: Nice approach — can we make corridor.window_ms and ward.backoff configurable per-deployment? Suggest default conservative values.
Author reply: yep, exposed both as runtime config with sane defaults; added validation in config/ward.yaml.

Sophie Lin: We should ensure the ward never reduces weight below tenant.min_guarantee — otherwise we risk unfair denial.
Author reply: added tenant.min_guarantee check and unit test; ward clamps to guarantee.

Ethan Grant (approval): Left one nit on log verbosity, otherwise LGTM.
Author reply: addressed nit, switched the ward logger to debug and reduced info churn.
SRE: ran chaos test in staging for regional partitioning, observed smoothing effect; two minor test flakiness issues addressed in second commit.

Security reviewer: no new surface for secrets, flagged config parsing safe.
Author reply: confirmed no KMS changes.
Release engineer: please note feature flag name 'ward.geo.enabled' for release notes.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash by Diego Morales after approvals. Shadow canary enabled for 48h post-merge; ops notified via #oncall. Change was released behind the ward.geo.enabled feature flag and then progressively enabled per rollout plan.
